_comment: A deliberate departure from an inherited title. plerdy-titles.json is a record of someone else's checklist and stays faithful to it; when this plugin's evidence cannot answer the borrowed sentence, the local title is declared here with the reason it differs. Keys are registry item ids; keys beginning with _ are metadata and never reach the generator. An override that matches the source title is not a no-op, it is a dead entry - delete it.

CI-002.title: Confirm Google Has Indexed the Audited URL
CI-002.why: URL Inspection answers for one URL, and requires: gsc keeps the item out of the per-page sampled pass, so it answers for the audited URL only. The Plerdy wording 'Ensure Important Content Is Indexed' claims the site's important content. Checking a set of important URLs needs a quota-aware GSC sampling feature that does not exist, so the plugin must not keep a title that implies it. The wording also has to stay distinct from CI-001 'Ensure URL Is Indexed', which asks whether this page can be indexed rather than whether Google has.

TE-181.title: Validate the Rendered DOM (W3C)
TE-181.why: TE-181 now sends the browser-built DOM to the Nu checker, while CI-017 keeps validating the HTML served at the URL. Keeping the inherited title on both would give two report rows the same name even when the two documents produce different verdicts.

TE-169.title: Provide Internal Links in the Served HTML
TE-169.why: The inherited title — Optimize JavaScript Rendering & Crawlability — promises a comparison between the served document and the rendered one. That comparison is MB-105, and scoring it three times is what the duplicate gate exists to stop. This item asserts something real and cheap about the served document, and its independently written fixture declaration already says so: every sampled page carries internal links in the served HTML. The title is brought into line with what both the assertion and the declaration mean.

LO-200.title: Publish Complete NAP in LocalBusiness Data
LO-200.why: The inherited title promises two off-site facts that a fetched page cannot establish: a business can have a complete Google Business Profile without linking it from the page, and visible on-page reviews are not evidence of its off-site review presence. LO-198 already asks whether LocalBusiness data exists anywhere on the site; this item grades the page-level fact the fetched data can prove: every LocalBusiness node present has a non-empty name, address and telephone.

TE-177.title: Provide a Title Element in the Served HTML
TE-177.why: The inherited title — Ensure No-JS Access & Crawlability — promises a comparison between the served document and the rendered one. That comparison is MB-105, and scoring it three times is what the duplicate gate exists to stop. This item asserts something real and cheap about the served document, and its independently written fixture declaration already says so: every sampled page carries a title element in the served HTML. The title is brought into line with what both the assertion and the declaration mean.
